prompt: Complete FixedWidthRecordReader.read so it reads 14-byte fixed-width records from a stream with readNBytes, trims the padding, and returns one "name=quantity" entry per complete record.
explanation: readNBytes(n) keeps reading until it has n bytes or the stream ends, which is exactly what fixed-width parsing needs -- a plain read(byte[]) could return a half record and leave you mid-field. A returned array shorter than the record size therefore means the stream ran out, which doubles as both the loop condition and the rule for discarding a truncated tail. Turning the bytes into a String with an explicit charset and then using substring keeps the column arithmetic readable.
hints: readNBytes returns an array whose length tells you how much it got; loop while that length is still 14.
Build one String from the 14 bytes with new String(chunk, StandardCharsets.US_ASCII), then substring(0, 10) and substring(10).
trim() removes both the right-hand spaces of the name and the left-hand padding of the quantity before Integer.parseInt.
